margin_framing.metric_basis_note: Privia defines Adjusted EBITDA Margin as Adjusted EBITDA as a percentage of Care Margin (10-Q document_id 130552), not of GAAP revenue. The 30% to 35% target is on that basis. On GAAP revenue the same EBITDA is about 6% (data_comps 6.47% forward, 6.10% LTM), which is why the screen flagged it as below the industry median; that comparison is not like for like.

statements.quote: We're well on our track to get to 25% EBITDA as a percentage of care margin, a long-term trajectory or targets for 30%-35%. I think we'll be there in the next few years.
statements.speaker: Parth Mehrotra
statements.doc_title: Privia Health Group Inc Q2 2025 Earnings Call

statements.quote: I mean, we are already approaching the low end of our long-term margin target, EBITDA care margin of 30%-35%. Our guidance this year, you know, gets us close to 29%. I think if we look at the next five years with everything we see that we can do with AI, I think we'll easily be, you know, at close to the high end, if not exceed the high end of that margin target.
statements.speaker: Parth Mehrotra
statements.doc_title: Privia Health Group Inc Q1 2026 Earnings Call

statements.quote: If you see our guidance, we expect to be 29% this year, EBITDA to care margin. It's pretty much very close to the 30%. Given all the work we are doing with different AI applications, with just scaling our business with growth, I think we're pretty confident that we can keep accreting that. There's no set timeline. We said over the next few years.
statements.speaker: Parth Mehrotra
statements.doc_title: Privia Health Group Inc Q2 2026 Earnings Call

street.gap_assumption: Margins are consensus EBITDA (data_financials summary, 2026-10-01) over consensus Care Margin (data_company_data Supplemental, fetched 2026-08-29), calendar fiscal years. No target year, so no formal gap. Street crosses the 30% low end in FY2028 (30.53%), reaches 32.74% FY2029 and 34.12% FY2030, 88 bps short of the 35% high end; versus FY2028 the gap to 35% is +447 bps. The street already models the range. On GAAP revenue consensus is 6.21% FY2026, 6.47% FY2027, 6.66% FY2028.
street.source: Baba data_financials consensus (Visible Alpha) and data_company_data Care margin (pid 14180700)

evidence_of_progress.note: Order [Q1 2026, Q2 2026], adjusted EBITDA as % of Care Margin. Q1 28.5% vs 25.6% (10-Q document_id 38653); Q2 28.3% vs 25.2%, +310 bps (CEO, document_id 130363; 8-K 0001759655-26-000061: adj. EBITDA $37.4M on Care Margin $132.1M vs $29.0M on $115.2M). FY2026 guidance raised to the high end on 2026-08-06, about 29%.

disqualifier_reason: No leadership catalyst in window: CEO Parth Mehrotra has been in seat since 2023-07-01 (internal promotion, 39 months) and CFO David Mountcastle since 2022-03-21; in-window events are two board additions and tuck-in acquisitions. The task premise of a 2025 CEO change is wrong. The 30% to 35% EBITDA-to-Care-Margin target is also already reflected in consensus (30.5% FY2028, 34.1% FY2030).
verdict: Not a GXO setup: cheap and down 30%, but the CEO is a 2023 internal successor, the margin target dates from the 2021 IPO and the street already models it.
open_questions: How much of the AI-driven cost story could push EBITDA to Care Margin above 35%, the only scenario not in consensus?
Is the de-rating driven by value-based care risk (V28, utilization) rather than margin skepticism?
What did the Evolent ACO deal cost and when did it close (no 8-K found)?
